bull.b: The sharp increase in TTM revenue shows meaningful commercial expansion and improving top-line traction. If the company can sustain this growth while controlling development costs, a larger revenue base could eventually support operating leverage and strengthen the pipeline’s economic potential.

Low debt relative to equity reduces near-term balance-sheet pressure and limits interest-related constraints on the business. This gives management more financial flexibility to fund development and absorb volatility, although continued losses could still weaken that position over time.

The narrower interim loss, supported by other operating income and tighter cost controls, indicates some progress in managing the cost base. Sustaining this improvement could reduce the pace of cash consumption while the company advances its early-stage development pipeline.

bear.b: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not yet self-funding its operations or development activities. Continued cash burn can require external financing, increasing dependence on capital markets and potentially limiting strategic flexibility if funding conditions weaken.

Negative gross profit and substantial operating losses show that revenue growth has not yet translated into a viable earnings model. Without clear operating leverage, additional revenue may continue to require significant investment, delaying profitability and increasing pressure on future funding needs.

Declining equity and assets alongside persistently negative returns indicate that ongoing losses are eroding the company’s financial base. If this pattern continues, the business may have less internal capacity to fund development and face greater dilution risk from future capital raising.
